Protests erupted at Delhi airport after two SpiceJet flights to Dubai were repeatedly rescheduled, leaving around 200 passengers facing prolonged delays, news agency PTI reported.Flights SG 5111 and SG 5105 were scheduled to depart for Dubai on Monday morning and evening, respectively. NEW DELHI: Bahujan Samaj Party chief Mayawati on Tuesday alleged that several candidates from her party were "forcibly defeated" in the municipal elections held in Rajasthan.In a social media post on X, Mayawati said that the BSP candidates lost by razor thin margins during recounts due to irregularities involving government machinery."In the local body elections held in Rajasthan, the BSP has also won 19 seats this time by getting its councillors elected, and many candidates have been forcibly defeated by small margins of votes during the recounting because of the irregularities of the government machinery. Article Title: ‘Serious lapse’: Air India CEO summoned after 3 foreigners 'skip' immigration check
Article Text:
What happened

NEW DELHI: Centre has summoned Air India CEO after three foreign nationals departed India without undergoing mandatory departure immigration clearance, news agency ANI reported, citing sources.Sources told ANI that the ministry of civil aviation has sought an explanation from the airline after the incident, terming it a "serious security and immigration-related lapse."This comes after the civil aviation ministry issued a show-cause notice to the airline over alleged procedural lapses that allowed three Italian passengers to board a connecting flight from Delhi without completing immigration formalities earlier this month.Three Italian nationals fly into Delhi from Amritsar on September 4 and then, within an hour, depart for Munich on a codeshare Lufthansa flight from Delhi airport without the mandatory immigration check.According to the ministry, the incident occurred during Air India's hub-and-spoke operation and involved a violation of the prescribed Standard Operating Procedure.Amritsar airport is among the airports where Air India operates flights under its ‘Hub-and-Spoke’ model.Under this arrangement, passengers complete immigration formalities at the airport of origin and can then travel to an overseas destination through a designated hub. At the hub airport, where the international flight departs, passengers are required only to undergo security checks before boarding.If a person is travelling from Amritsar via Delhi to a foreign destination, then Amritsar is the spoke and Delhi is the hub.In this case, the sources told PTI that the Italian nationals were issued boarding passes at Amritsar airport for Delhi as well as the Lufthansa flight to Munich.Meanwhile, home secretary Govind Mohan is expected to chair a meeting to discuss the incident on Tuesday. Secretary and additional secretary at the civil aviation ministry, director of Intelligence Bureau, additional secretary (UT and Foreigners) at the home ministry, Bureau of Immigration (BoI) commissioner, and Delhi airport CEO will attend the meeting, they added.The aviation ministry is also expected to make a presentation on ways to plug the gaps at the meeting.
Article Summary: Three italian nationals fly into delhi from amritsar on september 4 and then, within an hour, depart for munich on a codeshare lufthansa flight from delhi airport without the mandatory immigration check. Civil aviation ministry issued a show-cause notice to the airline over alleged procedural lapses.

Article Title: Xi's 5-point action plan for Brics may see red flags go up in India
Article Text:
Brics Summit 2026: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Chinese President Xi Jinping's statement on integrating markets and developing an open-source AI platform, along with other initiatives he proposed, is unlikely to enthuse policy circles here, given the wariness over such proposals from across the border.Ahead of China taking over presidency of Brics, Xi's speech at the concluding session of the summit is being seen as an indication that he would make a push for incorporation of these aspects into the agenda for next year's conference.For a long time, Brics has stayed away from becoming a trading bloc, and integrating markets through tariff cuts and investment protection regimes comes with the risk of opening markets to Chinese goods and companies with few guardrails, risking the development of homegrown technologies and players.India has maintained strict checks on Chinese investments, approving them on a case-by-case basis, and has refused to drop its guard despite the intense lobbying by sections of industry.The fear of Chinese cannibalisation of markets is not limited to India but is recognised globally - from Japan to Europe and the Americas - with countries trying to reduce their dependence and diversify sourcing. In fact, the rush of free trade agreements India has signed is partly driven by the strategy to diversify imports and govt's push to tap demand for Indian products through lower tariffs and reduced entry barriers.Ever since India walked out of RCEP in Nov 2019, fearing it would have to open the floodgates to Chinese imports, trade deals have become a crucial policy tool for India. It was China's dominance in RCEP that finally prompted India to opt out of the agreement, given that it had trade deals with countries such as Japan, South Korea and Asean members. Since then, India's portfolio has expanded to include FTAs with Australia, New Zealand, UAE, the UK, the EU and EFTA nations.The president's AI push in his five-point action plan, proposed Sunday, is among the biggest fears, given concerns about Chinese players and their development model. The push for Chinese LLMs, part of the proposals, is a sure-shot red flag and will be seen as an attempt to infiltrate countries amid global scrutiny of Chinese apps and technologies. India itself has blocked several apps and is on guard when it comes to allowing technologies in China-made cameras and other devices.Similarly, policymakers will be sceptical over the Chinese push for the SEZ initiative and the pitch to upgrade factories, especially when Belt and Road Initiative turned into a plan to corner key projects and use the funding to arm-twist governments into giving up control over the assets.
Article Summary: Chinese president xi jinping's statement on integrating markets and developing an open-source ai platform is unlikely to enthuse policy circles here. India has maintained strict checks on chinese investments, approving them on a case-by-case basis. The fear of chinese cannibalisation of markets is recognised globally - from japan to europe and the americas.

Article Title: India to export 654MW of power to Nepal daily till Dec 31
Article Text:
Nepal floods

NEW DELHI: Govt has agreed to export 654MW of electricity daily to flood-ravaged Nepal for 18 hours a day till Dec 31. The ministry of power Monday said the recent floods caused significant damage to hydropower infrastructure in Nepal, reducing its domestic power generation capacity and creating an additional requirement for electricity, reports Atul Mathur.Beginning Sunday, India started exporting up to 600MW electricity between midnight and 6pm to Nepal Electricity Authority through the Muzaffarpur-Dhalkebar 400 kV DC line and up to 54MW through the Tanakpur-Mahendranagar 132 kV SC line."The quantum of power to be exported from Jan 2027 will be reviewed in Dec," the ministry said in a statement, adding, "India remains committed to supporting Nepal and strengthening bilateral cooperation in the energy sector," the ministry added.Officials said floods in the Trishuli/Lhende Khola river basin on Aug 26 caused severe damage to infrastructure and disrupted some generating stations, following which Kathmandu requested India to advance the export mechanism, which otherwise begins in Oct and remains in place during the winter months.Nepal's generation capacity was reduced by nearly 550MW due to the damage."The approval will help Nepal meet its power requirements during this difficult period and further strengthen the close and long-standing energy cooperation between the two countries," an official said. India imports hydropower from Nepal during summer and exports electricity in the dry winter, when river flows fall and generation is impacted.

Officials said floods in the trishuli/lhende khola river basin on aug 26 caused severe damage to infrastructure and disrupted some generating stations. Article Title: ‘Partners, not rivals’: China FM Wang Yi reveals key PM Modi-Xi consensus

NEW DELHI: India and China should view each other as partners rather than rivals, Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi said on Monday, citing the consensus reached between president Xi Jinping and Prime Minister Narendra Modi during their meeting on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi.Wang said the two leaders held a “candid and in-depth exchange of views” on strategic and long-term issues concerning bilateral ties, according to news agency PTI. “The most important consensus they reached was that China and India should be partners,” he told Chinese official media.According to Wang, Xi said China and India could draw on each other's strengths, support one another, help each other succeed and pursue common development. The two leaders also agreed to maintain peace and tranquillity in border areas and support each other during their respective BRICS chairmanships.The Chinese foreign ministry said the relationship had moved from a “restart” to a “renewed elevation” under the strategic guidance of the two leaders. Wang said areas of cooperation were expanding, trade had reached record levels and people-to-people exchanges were becoming more active.Wang also quoted PM Modi as saying India was ready to be “a partner, not an adversary” to China and viewed each other’s development “as an opportunity rather than a challenge”. He said PM had reaffirmed that India’s approach to China was independent of third-party influence.The two leaders, according to Wang, agreed to deepen political trust, appropriately manage differences and strengthen cooperation in areas including cultural exchanges and direct air connectivity. They also agreed to coordinate more closely through the United Nations, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation and the G20, while advancing cooperation among Global South countries.The Indian foreign ministry’s account of the meeting highlighted the need for a “strategic and long-term perspective” in managing bilateral ties. According to MEA, PM Modi said differences should not become disputes and that relations should be guided by “three mutuals” — mutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interest.PM Modi also stressed that peace and tranquillity along the border remained essential for the broader relationship and called for adherence to existing agreements and understandings. Both sides backed a “fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable resolution” of the boundary question.On trade, the leaders discussed structural imbalances, supply-chain concerns and the need for “meaningful and predictable market access”. They also welcomed progress in people-to-people ties and called for greater cultural, business and travel links.Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Beijing would work with New Delhi to implement the understandings reached by the leaders and “make the cooperation list longer”.She said, "As the two leaders have charted the course for the future development of the bilateral ties, China will work with India to implement the important common understandings reached between the two leaders."With China set to assume the BRICS chairmanship in 2027, both sides are expected to build on the latest engagement.
Article Summary: China and india should view each other as partners rather than rivals, says chinese foreign minister. Wang yi cites consensus reached between president xi jinping and prime minister narendra modi during their meeting on the sidelines of the brics summit in new delhi.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Monday launched a sharp attack on the Centre over the country’s economic situation, saying that while Prime Minister Narendra Modi claims “all is well”, the reality on the ground is marked by soaring prices and shrinking incomes."The PM keeps saying सब चंगा सी (all is well), but actually सब महँगा सी (everything is expensive)," Ramesh said in a post on X.Highlighting the pressure on household budgets, Congress MP Ramesh cited the Wholesale Price Index (WPI), writing, "Official data just released shows that for four consecutive months now the WPI (Wholesale Price Index) inflation has been hovering around 10%. Prices of all essential commodities have continued their upward rise causing huge hardships to crores of families."Ramesh further cited findings by the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE) to highlight the distress in the labour market, particularly in rural areas."To compound the misery, according to CMIE data, inflation-adjusted wages have also been consistently falling with a 5.7% drop since April. Rural India has seen a massive 9% decline - even in nominal terms, rural wages have fallen," Ramesh stated.Ramesh’s remarks came after the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) for all commodities stood at 110.8 in August 2026, with annual wholesale inflation rising to 9.92 per cent year-on-year (YoY), according to official data released by the Ministry of Commerce & Industry.The figure marked a marginal increase from July 2026, when headline wholesale inflation stood at 9.78 per cent. The all-commodities index also edged up from 110.0 recorded in the previous month.The rise reflected price pressures across major industrial and energy segments. Fuel and power recorded the sharpest increase, with YoY inflation accelerating to 22.93 per cent in August from 20.05 per cent in July.In contrast, inflation in primary articles moderated to 7.76 per cent from 8.52 per cent in the preceding month. Inflation in manufactured products edged up to 8.37 per cent from 8.29 per cent over the same period.

NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh Monday hailed New Delhi Brics declaration passed unanimosly, saying the unison adaptation was an "statement of India’s growing global influence" under Prime Minister Narendra Modi Calling "inclusive and human-centric approach" an hallmark of the summit, the defence minister laid emphasis on how the bloc put Global South "at the centre, not at the margins, championing a more inclusive, representative and balanced world order"."Rooted in our civilisational ethos of Vasudhaiv Kutumbkam, India has once again shown that leadership is not about having the loudest voice, but the strongest consensus," the Union minister said, adding: "As India leads, the world listens."In a dramatic echo of the 2023 G20 summit in New Delhi, Brics countries agreed on a joint declaration after intensive negotiations that continued until 4 am on Saturday. The talks were complicated by differences between Iran and the UAE over the West Asia conflict. An earlier meeting of Brics foreign ministers under India’s presidency had also ended without a joint statement.The 140-paragraph New Delhi Declaration was announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi after a rare meeting between Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on the sidelines of the summit.The meeting took place as the conflict continued and helped ease the differences threatening consensus.The declaration used carefully balanced language to address the concerns of both countries. It expressed serious concern over deliberate attacks on civilian infrastructure and peaceful nuclear facilities operating under full International Atomic Energy Agency safeguards, describing such actions as violations of international law and relevant IAEA resolutions. The wording amounted to an implicit criticism of US and Israeli strikes on Iran and was important in securing Tehran’s approval.The leaders also recalled their respective national positions on West Asia and stressed the need to maintain the smooth movement of global trade, supply chains and energy in line with international law.Official sources said India conducted prolonged negotiations at several levels to bridge the differences between Iran and the UAE. Other member-states also supported the effort, keen to ensure that the summit ended with a joint declaration rather than another failure to reach consensus.The agreement recalled the last-minute G20 declaration adopted in New Delhi in 2023 during the Russia-Ukraine war. That statement used carefully worded language urging countries not to use force to seize territory without directly naming Russia.

Article Title: “It just took a lot out of me": Gisele Bündchen opens up about severe panic attacks and the life lessons she learned after Tom Brady divorce
Article Text:
Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen (Instagram and Getty Images)

Gisele Bündchen reveals how panic attacks changed her life

Gisele Bündchen has spent much of her life in the public eye, but some of her hardest battles happened away from the cameras. The former supermodel has opened up about the panic attacks she faced in her early 20s, describing the experience as a turning point that changed how she viewed her body, choices and future. Years later, after her marriage to Tom Brady ended, those lessons continued to shape the way she approached life and wellness.Bündchen entered modelling as a teenager and quickly found herself living at a pace few people could sustain. Success brought travel, work and global attention, but the pressure also took a toll.By her early 20s, she was dealing with severe panic attacks for around two years. Instead of simply trying to push through them, Bündchen eventually began looking at what was happening beneath the surface.She recently reflected on that period during an appearance on the i-D podcast. Her description was not simply about anxiety. It was about losing touch with herself and then slowly finding her way back.“I feel like there is many deaths and rebirths in my life,” she shared on the i-D podcast, answering a fan's question. “I think when you're 46, you definitely have gone through a few of those, but I would say one of the most intense ones for me was when I had panic attacks, and I was dealing with it in my early 20s for about two years.I think I was living so much outside of myself, almost detached and trying to be a pleaser.“It's when I really had to dive deep, and I discovered who I was, and I realized that my body was my temple and I could be the director of my own movie, that I could create my life, and that was very powerful moment. So I'm very grateful. That's why I say, ‘What doesn't kill you makes you stronger.'”That period became a foundation for Bündchen's approach to wellness. She later made changes to her diet and daily habits, placing greater importance on health rather than simply maintaining the image expected of her.Bündchen's personal journey took another major turn through her marriage to Tom Brady. The couple married in 2009 and became parents to Benjamin and Vivian. Their relationship brought family life into an already demanding world of professional sports and modelling.Their divorce in 2022 marked another difficult transition. Brady later acknowledged how deeply the separation affected him, including its impact on his football career.“It was a challenge,” Brady told FOX News. “It just took a lot out of me in terms of my ability to continue to play.”Bündchen also spoke about the emotional weight of seeing a future she had imagined take a different path.“It's tough because you imagine your life was going to be a certain way, and you did everything you could, you know?” she told Vanity Fair.Rather than allowing those experiences to define her, Bündchen continued building a life around health and self-awareness. Her 2024 book,, further explored those ideas and encouraged readers to think differently about their relationship with food and wellbeing.“This is my temple,” Bündchen said on GMA. “I only get one, so I how can I nourish it? And how can I love it? If it's not nourishing me, then I'm not going to eat it. I think that's the number one thing. Making a commitment to your health.”For Bündchen, the biggest lesson from those difficult chapters appears to be ownership. Fame, marriage and major life changes brought challenges she could not always control. But she found a way to regain control over how she cared for herself and what came next.
Article Summary: Gisele bündchen has opened up about the panic attacks she faced in her early 20s. She described the experience as a turning point that changed how she viewed her body, choices and future. Years later, after her marriage to tom brady ended, those lessons continued to shape the way she approached life.

Article Title: 'Was laughing': Video shows Indian-origin woman, friend moments before NYC subway train ran over them
Article Text:
An Indian origin woman and her friend were tragically hit by a subway train in NYC.

What happened on the tracks?

Why were they on the tracks?

Who were Malaika Chitre and Navam Kaul?

Indian-origin woman and her friend, both 24-year-old, from New Jersey were fatally struck by a New York City subway train early Sunday after they were seen sitting on the tracks at a Manhattan station. Investigators are trying to determine how and why they ended up in the path of the approaching train.Malaika Chitre and Navam Kaul, both recent Rutgers University graduates, were on the tracks at Spring Street station in Lower Manhattan shortly after 3 am when a southbound No 4 train entered the station. The train operator saw the pair and tried to stop, but was unable to prevent the collision. Both were pronounced dead at the scene. Around 100 passengers were later evacuated from the train, according to reports.The circumstances surrounding the deaths remain unclear. Investigators are examining whether Kaul first fell or went onto the tracks and Chitre followed in an attempt to help him, whether intoxication played a role, or whether the possibility of suicide should be considered.An incident report obtained by the New York Daily News said the train operator told supervisors that she saw the man and woman sitting on the tracks as the train approached.She attempted to stop the train, but it was too late.The report said Chitre appeared to be laughing and pulling Kaul towards her when the train struck them. Separately, law-enforcement sources told the New York Post that Kaul may have fallen or made his way onto the tracks before Chitre went down after him.Video circulating on social media also appeared to show the pair sitting together on the tracks shortly before the train arrived. AmNewYork reported that the operator activated the emergency brake but could not stop the train in time.The medical examiner has not yet released an official determination explaining the circumstances of the deaths.One possibility being examined is that Kaul ended up on the tracks first and Chitre went down to help him.Police sources told the New York Post that it was not immediately clear whether Kaul had fallen or climbed down. Chitre appeared to try to pull him towards her before the train hit them.If that account is confirmed, Chitre may have gone onto the tracks in an attempt to rescue her friend, rather than intentionally placing herself in the path of the train.However, investigators have not established what happened immediately before the pair were seen on the tracks.Investigators are also looking into whether one or both of them were intoxicated and may have been too impaired or disoriented to recognise the danger posed by the approaching train, according to law-enforcement sources.The footage showing the pair apparently remaining on the tracks as the train approached has raised questions about whether they understood what was happening around them. But there has been no official finding that alcohol or drugs were involved, and toxicology results, if any, have not been made public.Suicide has also been posed as a possible explanation.No suicide note was found at the scene, according to sources cited by the New York Post. However, the absence of a note does not by itself establish how the pair came to be on the tracks, and investigators have not concluded that their deaths were intentional.At present, there is no publicly established motive for why the two were on the tracks.Chitre and Kaul were longtime friends who attended Rutgers University around the same time and graduated in 2024.Chitre, from the Dayton section of South Brunswick, New Jersey, graduated from Rutgers with a degree in public health and a minor in business administration. She was working as a quality operations specialist at pharmaceutical company Acadia Pharmaceuticals and had recently begun pursuing a Doctor of Pharmacy degree at Temple University.Kaul, from Sayreville, New Jersey, graduated from Rutgers Business School with a degree in finance. He had been working as a financial data analyst at Bloomberg since 2025.The two were part of the same social circles and South Asian community around Rutgers, according to people who knew them. Rajnikant Pipalia, whose son was a close friend of Kaul, told the New York Post that the pair had grown up in the same social world and remained part of the same wider group of friends.Their deaths came as they were beginning their professional lives.
Article Summary: Malaika chitre and navam kaul were on the tracks at spring street station in lower manhattan shortly after 3 am when a southbound no 4 train entered the station. The train operator saw the pair and tried to stop, but was unable to prevent the collision. Around 100 passengers were later evacuated from the train, according to reports.

Article Title: Scotland, Northern Ireland and Wales sign historic MoU to break away from UK
Article Text:
Scottish first minister John Swinney, his Welsh counterpart Rhun ap Iorwerth and Northern Ireland’s Michelle O’Neill signed the MoU at a summit in Cardiff.

LONDON: Elected representatives of three devolved UK legislatures – Scotland, Northern Ireland and Wales – signed a historic pact on Monday, declaring their intent to break free of Westminster’s control.“The political landscape across these islands is changing. For the first time ever, there are first ministers in Scotland, in Wales and in the North of Ireland who are all committed to independence from the United Kingdom. For people watching around the world, there could be no clearer sign that Westminster’s time is coming to an end,” states the MoU.Scottish first minister John Swinney, his Welsh counterpart Rhun ap Iorwerth and Northern Ireland’s Michelle O’Neill signed the MoU at a summit in Cardiff. Sinn Fein president Mary Lou McDonald, leader of the opposition in Ireland, was the fourth signatory.“Our nations have the right to self-determination: No Westminster govt has the right to block democracy or undermine the principle that our people will decide their own future,” says the MoU.Plaid Cymru’s victory at the Senedd (Welsh parliament) elections in May ended Labour’s unbroken control of the Welsh govt since devolution began in 1999.It meant that the largest parties in all three devolved parliaments of the UK were pro-independence for the first time.“Each of our nations has the right to determine its own future, through democratic means and in accordance with the wishes of its people. We call for the British govt to prepare for, plan and facilitate constitutional change in each jurisdiction,” the agreement states.The MoU commits the parties to strengthening cooperation in areas such as the economy and energy resources, backed by a consensus that the future of these nations belongs in the European Union.UK PM Andy Burnham believes strongly in the UK and is focused on easing the cost-of-living crisis rather than on “constitutional debates”, Downing Street said.Conservative shadow Scottish secretary Harriet Cross described the meeting as “a separatist summit” and “performative photo call”.
Article Summary: Scottish first minister john swinney, his welsh counterpart rhun ap iorwerth and northern ireland’s michelle o’neill signed the mou. Sinn fein president mary lou mcdonald, leader of the opposition in ireland, was the fourth signatory.

Article Title: 3 UP youths missing in Russia; told kin ‘forced to fight against Ukraine’
Article Text:
While UP authorities assured families of inquiries and assistance, relatives await their safe repatriation.

(With inputs from Sudeep Lavania in Agra and Sachin Sharma in Shamli)





AGRA/SHAMLI: Amid the Russia-Ukraine conflict, families of three young men from western Uttar Pradesh are living in despair after losing contact with their sons in Moscow.The youths, who travelled to Russia on study visas last year, reportedly claimed before going silent that local authorities confiscated their passports and forced them into military service.The missing youths are Himanshu Sharma (24) and Shakti Punder (23), both from Muzaffarnagar, and Ashu Saini (25) from Shamli district. The three men were sharing a room in the Russian capital Moscow and were pursuing a Russian language course.According to relatives, the last contact with the students came on July 30, when brief phone calls were made before their lines went dead and their phones switched off. Himanshu Sharma went to Russia on a student visa to study and take up permissible part-time work.His cousin, Priyanshu Sharma, told reporters, “His passport was due to expire this year. Since that last call on July 30, we have called his number several times with no response. We suspect he could be forced into the Russian Army.”Similarly, Shakti Punder’s father reported speaking to him last on the same day, after which all communication ceased.Ashu Saini hailed from Hasanpur Lohari village in Shamli’s Thanabhawan area and left for Russia in April 2026.His sister, Anshul, recalled a hurried 30-second final conversation where he briefly mentioned he was fine before hanging up.Ashu’s father, Rakesh Kumar, a farmer, has formally appealed to the Prime Minister’s Office seeking his son’s safe return.Following desperate pleas from the families, appeals were dispatched to ministry of external affairs (MEA). In response, MEA informed the families that India’s embassy in Moscow has actively intervened.“The embassy has taken up the matter with the Russian authorities concerned. They have reportedly joined the Russian army; the embassy has sought details of their whereabouts. The embassy is separately taking up their case,” the MEA stated in its reply to the families of the youths.In July, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal acknowledged that approximately 24 Indian citizens—recruited through fraudulent or non-transparent means—remain stuck serving within the ranks of Russian army as the war in Ukraine persists.While local authorities in Uttar Pradesh have assured grieving families that inquiries are underway and assistance will be extended, relatives continue to wait anxiously for their safe repatriation.
Article Summary: Families of three young men from western uttar pradesh are living in despair after losing contact with their sons in moscow. The youths, who travelled to russia on study visas last year, reportedly claimed before going silent that local authorities confiscated their passports and forced them into military service.

Article Title: 'Even Donald Trump is copying us': DK Shivakumar says US $5,000 promise 'inspired' by Congress guarantees
Article Text:
Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar stated Donald Trump is copying Congress's guarantee schemes





BENGALURU: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Monday said even US President Donald Trump was “copying” the Congress government ’s guarantee schemes, while highlighting what he described as their popularity among people.Speaking in Bengaluru, Shivakumar said the Congress government’s welfare guarantees had become a “blockbuster” and drew a comparison with Trump’s recent promise to give every adult American $5,000 if Republicans retain control of the House and Senate in the November midterm elections.Trump has renewed his proposal for a $5,000 “dividend” for every adult American, saying the US government could afford the payments because it was collecting large amounts of revenue.“I don't know but it's easy if the Republicans win. $5,000 to all adults in the country and we can easily handle that because we're taking in so much money,” Trump told reporters in Ireland on Sunday, according to reports.Trump had first unveiled the proposal at a Republican Party convention in Dallas. He linked the proposed payments to what he described as trillions of dollars flowing into the US.
Article Summary: Karnataka chief minister dk shivakumar stated donald trump is copying congress's guarantee schemes. He drew a comparison with trump’s recent promise to give every adult american $5,000 if republicans retain control of the house and senate in the november midterm elections.

Article Title: ‘Working on Iran’s NDB membership’: Araghchi reveals Brics bank push, calls Modi-Pezeshkian meet ‘strong’
Article Text:
Iranian foreign minister joins Brics summit in New Delhi

NEW DELHI: Iran has stepped up its bid to join the New Development Bank (NDB), with foreign minister Abbas Araghchi saying Tehran has secured support from some countries and is now working to complete the requirements for membership.Araghchi, who is in New Delhi for the 18th Brics Summit, also described Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian ’s meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi as a “strong”, while highlighting Iran’s expanding engagement with Brics members and other countries.Speaking to Iranian news outlet SNN Iran on Saturday, Araghchi said Tehran was actively pursuing membership of the NDB.“We are working on that today, and some countries are supportive, and they are in the process of fulfilling the necessary requirements,” he said.Iran’s bid to join the NDB was announced last month by Central Bank of Iran governor Abdolnaser Hemmati, according to TV Brics, which cited Iranian media reports.Araghchi also highlighted discussions among Brics leaders on greater use of national currencies, on Friday. Referring to the meetings, he said, “Mr Putin, Mr Modi, and Dr Pezeshkian, especially regarding the use of local currencies and national currencies, had a conversation that caught the attention of the world and attracted a lot of news coverage.”He said Saturday’s main summit would be accompanied by a series of bilateral meetings involving Pezeshkian.“Today, the main session of the summit will begin. Along with that, the President had bilateral meetings. Yesterday, there was a very strong meeting with India; today with Malaysia as well, and with Ethiopia, which is an important country in Africa,” Araghchi said.“Bilateral issues are being raised, regional issues are being raised, and praise be to God, the Islamic Republic of Iran's relations are expanding with the collection of Islamic countries and the countries of the region, and this is evident in all the meetings,” he added.Pezeshkian also used his meetings in New Delhi to push for closer economic cooperation within Brics. During his meeting with Ethiopian prime minister Abiy Ahmed Ali, he called for stronger economic and financial ties among Brics member countries and said the US presence in West Asia was a factor contributing to bloodshed.In his meeting with Malaysian prime minister Anwar Ibrahim, Pezeshkian said the region did not need a “policeman” and argued that Middle East security should be ensured by countries in the region. He also said Iran would seek to strengthen and rationalise its relations with Muslim and neighbouring countries, while emphasising that Iran is a peace-seeking country.Earlier on Friday, PM Modi also held a bilateral meeting with the Iranian president, continuing discussions from their meeting on the sidelines of the SCO Summit in Bishkek.According to the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), the two leaders reviewed various aspects of India-Iran ties, with PM Modi thanking Iran for its regular, high-level participation in Brics-related meetings despite challenging circumstances.PM Modi also thanked Pezeshkian for participating in the Leaders’ Session of the Brics Business Forum and highlighted the grouping’s potential to build “resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability” among countries of the Global South.The two leaders also discussed the conflict in West Asia. PM Modi reiterated India’s position that all issues should be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy, while stressing the need for continued efforts towards lasting peace and stability, including freedom of navigation and commerce and the safety of seafarers.In a post on X, PM Modi described the meeting as a continuation of their discussions in Bishkek.“From Bishkek to Delhi, the productive discussions continue. Happy to have met Dr Masoud Pezeshkian, the President of Iran. This visit is more special because it is his first visit to India. We talked about the India-Iran friendship. We believe that we should move forward with a long-term and win-win strategy. The prevailing situation in the region was also discussed.India remains steadfast in its commitment to the pursuit of enduring peace,” PM Modi said.On the opening day of the Brics Summit on Saturday, Pezeshkian also met president Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi. Iran joined the expanded Brics grouping in January 2024, alongside Egypt, Ethiopia, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.
Article Summary: Iran has stepped up its bid to join the new development bank (ndb) foreign minister abbas araghchi said tehran has secured support from some countries. He also described iranian president masoud pezeshkian ’s meeting with prime minister narendra modi as a “strong’ the prevailing situation in the region was also discussed, pm modi said.

Article Title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei responds to former employee who resigned 'warning' that AI could kill all of us, says: I agree with Jacob Coxon on ...
Article Text:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei

What did Jacob Coxon say about AI killing humans

Dario Amodei says he agrees with Jacob Coxon

Why Dario Amodei does not give one AI extinction percentage

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has responded to former researcher Jacob Coxon’s resignation, who left the AI company earlier this month and warned that rapidly developing AI systems could “kill us all by the end of the decade. ” In a CNN interview, Dario Amodei said he “agree[s] with Jacob much more than I disagree with him”, while making clear that Coxon was not specifically accusing Anthropic of acting irresponsibly. Instead, Amodei said Jacob Coxon was warning about the wider AI industry moving too fast. During the interview, Dario Amodei also explained why he no longer prefers giving a single percentage for the risk of AI causing catastrophic harm, saying the focus should be on choosing the right path for AI development.Jacob Coxon, who worked on pretraining research at both Anthropic and OpenAI, resigned from Anthropic earlier this month. In a post on X, he said the companies were not acting responsibly and warned that the AI industry was moving towards self-improving superintelligence.Coxon wrote that AI developers were “racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.” He also said people building AI “earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.”His post quickly drew widespread attention, with CNN reporting that it was seen by more than 40 million people.Asked by CNN's Anderson Cooper whether he believes AI could kill all humans and what probability he would put on that outcome, Amodei did not reject Coxon's concern.“It's funny, I agree with Jacob much more than I disagree with him,” Amodei said.He then explained why he viewed Coxon's resignation differently from a direct criticism of Anthropic.“It's an interesting resignation, because when he left, he said, you know, I think Anthropic is the most responsible player, right? I think Anthropic is the most aware of these issues. He wasn't calling out us. He was calling out the dynamic of the industry as a whole, moving too fast.”Dario Amodei was also asked to put a number on the possibility of AI causing catastrophic harm. He said he used to discuss AI risks in terms of a single probability because it was an easy way to explain the issue. He now believes that approach can hide the different ways AI development could unfold.“I think there's some chance that things go wrong, but, you know, but it's not, it's not all that high,” Amodei said. He then explained that the more useful question is what paths the AI industry takes.“But again, I think it's more illuminating to think in terms of, you know, how do you decompose those probabilities? What are the paths in which things go well, and what are the paths in which things go poorly?”Rather than saying there is a fixed 10% or 20% chance that AI could cause a disaster, Amodei said the outcome depends on decisions made by companies and governments. “And so instead of saying, you know, it's a 10% chance, that sounds like it's a roll of the dice,” he said.He added:“I think it's much more illuminating to say, well, that forks into different paths. And if we take the right path, then the chance of something going wrong is very low. If we take the wrong path, then the chance of something going wrong could be, could be even higher than that.”“So let's focus on our agency, and our ability to take the right paths instead of the wrong paths,” he said.
Article Summary: Anthropic ceo dario amodei responds to jacob coxon's resignation. Coxon warned that rapidly developing ai systems could ‘kill us all by the end of the decade’ amodei says he agrees with coxon more than he disagrees with him.

Article Title: Donald Trump called Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang mid-interview and tells everyone he cannot take him on ...
Article Text:
Donald Trump's position

A debate already roiling Silicon Valley

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s response

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's appearance at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles took an unexpected turn when US President Donald Trump phoned in mid-conversation, using the moment to publicly dismiss growing concerns about AI posing an existential risk. According to a report by Business Insider, at the All-In Summit the interview of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was interrupted by a phone call from Trump. The interruption began with a bit of stage comedy. As Nvidia CEO scrambled to get Trump patched through on speakerphone, the moment was framed as the president now addressing the entire planet — with a joke about the irony of Huang being able to design the world's most advanced computer chips, yet needing help simply getting a phone connected to a speaker. "See, the great thing about life is that Jensen can develop the most complex computer chip in the world that nobody can copy for 10 years, but he can't figure it out to put me on speaker," said Trump.Speaking via speakerphone, Trump also dismissed the fears of artificial intelligence as alarmist, declaring, “The robots will not be taking over.” He further added that while caution is necessary, the US should not halt AI advancement.Trump described AI doomerism as a “hoax,” reiterating his stance later on Truth Social: “Breaking another Hoax That AI is going to take over, consume, and destroy the World.” His remarks came amid growing debate in Silicon Valley over AI safety, following whistleblower Jacob Coxon’s resignation from Anthropic, where he warned that AI could “kill us all by the end of the decade.”The interruption landed in the middle of an already heated industry conversation about AI safety. The debate intensified after Jacob Coxon, a former Anthropic researcher, announced his resignation from the lab last week, writing on social media that people building the technology believe it could pose a threat to humanity's survival within the decade.During his talk, Huang struck a more measured tone than Trump's, praising Coxon for speaking out about AI safety while also pushing back on the broader idea that AI represents an existential threat, calling that particular framing unscientific. He said AI safety is paramount, while maintaining that the U.S. can continue moving quickly on AI development without sacrificing safety, arguing the country is capable of leading in AI while still doing so responsibly.Huang drew a clear distinction between Coxon's decision to speak up and the broader predictions being made about AI's future. He said he considers whistleblowing about problems inside a company to be legitimate, but views scientific-sounding predictions about the future as considerably less credible, since he argued they aren't actually grounded in science. He added that he doesn't personally know what Coxon witnessed while at Anthropic, and suggested that frontier AI labs more broadly are in the midst of a difficult transition from primarily research-driven organizations into engineering-focused ones.
Article Summary: Us president donald trump interrupts nvidia ceo jensen huang's talk at all-in summit in los angeles. Trump calls ai doomerism a 'hoax' and dismisses fears of robots taking over as 'alarmist' comments come amid growing debate in silicon valley over ai safety.
